title: Debugging C/C++ Correctness: UB, Sanitizers, Valgrind, gdb & Static Analysis
summary: Quick revision notes on common C/C++ undefined behavior and the toolchain used to catch it: sanitizers, Valgrind, gdb, strict warnings and static analysis. Ends with a cheat sheet of flags and commands.

chapters.title: Undefined Behavior: What It Is and Why It Bites
points: Undefined behavior (UB): the standard places no requirements on the program, so the compiler may assume it never happens and optimize on that assumption
UB is not a crash guarantee: it can appear to work, misbehave only at -O2, or break after a compiler upgrade
Unspecified behavior (e.g. argument evaluation order) picks one of several valid results; implementation-defined behavior (e.g. sizeof(int)) is documented; UB has no valid result
Optimizer consequence: after `if (p->x)` the compiler may drop a later `if (!p)` null check, since p was already dereferenced
UB is a property of the program execution, not of one line: a single bad input path poisons the whole run, so passing tests prove nothing

chapters.title: The Four Common UB Families
points: Out of bounds: reading or writing past an array or heap buffer (`a[n]` on `int a[n]`); also forming a pointer more than one past the end is UB
Signed integer overflow is UB (`INT_MAX + 1`), while unsigned overflow wraps modulo 2^N and is defined; the compiler may fold `x + 1 > x` to true
Use after free / double free / returning a pointer to a local (dangling stack pointer): memory may still look valid until it is reused
Uninitialized reads: locals and malloc'd memory hold indeterminate values; calloc or `= {0}` initializes, malloc does not
Other frequent ones: null dereference, shift by >= width or by a negative amount, data races on non-atomic variables, strict aliasing violations

chapters.title: Sanitizers: ASan, UBSan, TSan
points: Sanitizers instrument the binary at compile time and report at runtime with a stack trace; build with `-g -O1` and `-fno-omit-frame-pointer` for readable traces
ASan (`-fsanitize=address`) catches heap/stack/global out-of-bounds, use-after-free, double free and leaks (LeakSanitizer); about 2x slowdown, 2-3x memory
UBSan (`-fsanitize=undefined`) catches signed overflow, bad shifts, null deref, misaligned access; add `-fno-sanitize-recover=all` to abort on the first error instead of continuing
TSan (`-fsanitize=thread`) detects data races; cannot be combined with ASan in one binary, so use separate builds; about 5-15x slowdown
MSan (`-fsanitize=memory`, Clang only) finds uninitialized reads but needs all code including libs instrumented; combine ASan+UBSan freely in one build, and run the test suite or CI under them

chapters.title: Valgrind, gdb and Core Dumps
points: Valgrind memcheck needs no recompile (build with `-g`): `valgrind --leak-check=full --track-origins=yes ./prog` reports invalid reads/writes, uninitialized use and leaks; 10-50x slowdown
Reading Valgrind output: 'definitely lost' is a real leak; 'still reachable' is usually fine; `--track-origins=yes` shows where an uninitialized value came from
Valgrind vs ASan: Valgrind works on unmodified binaries but is slower and misses stack/global overflows; ASan is faster and catches more but needs a rebuild
gdb basics: `gdb ./prog`, `run`, `bt` (backtrace), `frame N`, `print var`, `break file.c:42`, `next` / `step` / `continue`, `watch var`, `info locals`
Crashes without a debugger: `ulimit -c unlimited` then `gdb ./prog core` and `bt`; build with `-g` and without optimization (-O0) for accurate variable values

chapters.title: Warnings as Errors and Static Analysis
points: Baseline flags: `-Wall -Wextra -Wpedantic -Werror` (GCC/Clang) and `/W4 /WX` (MSVC); fail the build so warnings never accumulate
Useful extras: `-Wshadow -Wconversion -Wsign-compare -Wnull-dereference -Wformat=2`; `-Wuninitialized` and `-Wmaybe-uninitialized` need optimization enabled to work well
Static analyzers find bugs without running the code: clang-tidy (`clang-tidy file.cpp -- -std=c++20`), cppcheck, `gcc -fanalyzer`, clang `--analyze`
Static vs dynamic: static analysis covers all paths but gives false positives; sanitizers and Valgrind have no false positives but only see executed paths, so use both

Mistakes: silencing a warning with a cast or `#pragma` instead of fixing it; applying `-Werror` to third-party headers (use `-isystem`); testing only in debug builds where optimizer-exposed UB stays hidden

chapters.title: Cheat Sheet: Flags and Commands
points: Debug build: `g++ -g -O1 -fno-omit-frame-pointer -Wall -Wextra -Werror -fsanitize=address,undefined prog.cpp`
Thread build: `g++ -g -O1 -fsanitize=thread prog.cpp` (never combined with ASan); env options such as `ASAN_OPTIONS=detect_leaks=1:halt_on_error=1`
Valgrind: `valgrind --leak-check=full --track-origins=yes --error-exitcode=1 ./prog`
gdb: `gdb -ex run --args ./prog`; `bt`, `frame N`, `print x`, `watch x`, `break f`, `info locals`, `up` / `down`, `core` files via `ulimit -c unlimited`

Which tool for which bug: out-of-bounds or use-after-free → ASan; overflow or shifts → UBSan; races → TSan; uninitialized → MSan or Valgrind; any crash → gdb backtrace; code smells → clang-tidy / cppcheck
